title: The Mongolian ger: lattice walls, roof ring and poles, sheep-wool felt, south-facing door, seasonal moves

sources.title: Next Great Travel Writer: The Steppes of Mongolia
Counting the uncounted: how the Mongolian nomadic survey is leaving no one behind

facts.text: A ger is a round tent: a wooden frame covered with felt, used by Mongolian herders.
Its lattice walls fold like an accordion and are set up in a circle.
Two posts in the middle hold up a central ring at the top of the roof.
Dozens of thin roof poles run from the central ring out to the walls.
The frame is covered with felt made from sheep’s wool, then cloth or canvas.
Herders use one layer of felt in summer and several layers in winter.
A small wood-burning stove inside heats the ger.
The door of a ger faces south.
Experienced herders can put up a ger within a short time (well under a day).
Herders move with the seasons to find fresh pasture near water.
Many Mongolian herders keep sheep and sell wool, milk and meat.

notes: 混合題 mixed-advanced-04 第 4 組用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。搭建所需時間各來源不一（s1 說熟手 30 分鐘；旅遊資料多寫數小時），選文只寫一家人早餐後拆、午餐前在新營地搭好（含搬運），不寫確切時數。門朝南只有 s1 一個來源，寫成牧民口述的家中習慣。Text A 的旅遊作家、Text B 的牧民一家都是虛構人物。
